notes:
Very comprehensive answer from BrazeAI on the "Users have clicked 'yes' to my push primer IAM but I can't send them pushes" question:
"Reasons Why Push Notifications May Not Be Sent Despite Users Clicking 'Yes' on Push Primer IAM
Manual Code Removal: Ensure that any existing push notification integration code that requests push permission is removed or modified so that the in-app message (IAM) push primer is the first to request permission. Duplicate or premature requests can interfere with push registration.
Platform-Specific Permissions: On Android 13 and above, if a user denies push permission twice, further prompts are blocked by the OS, requiring manual enabling in device settings. On Android 12 and earlier, push is opted-in by default, so implementing push primers is not recommended.
Push Token Registration: After users accept push permissions, the device must register and provide a valid push token to Braze. Without a valid push token, pushes cannot be sent.
Push Subscription State: Users must be in the 'Subscribed' or 'Opted-In' push subscription state and have foreground push enabled. If a user has unsubscribed or disabled push in device settings, they will not be push enabled.
Automatic Suppression: If you are using the no-code push primer button action, the Braze SDK automatically suppresses the IAM on devices that already have an active push token, but if you have custom logic or deep links instead, the SDK may not detect the push primer correctly.
Targeting and Segmentation: Verify that your push campaign targets the correct users and devices that have accepted push permissions and are push enabled. Incorrect segmentation filters may exclude eligible users.
Push Certificate and API Key Configuration: Ensure that your push credentials, such as APNs certificates for iOS or Firebase Cloud Messaging API keys for Android, are correctly configured in Braze.
App State and Integration: Confirm that the app is properly integrated with Braze SDK and that the user is logged into the relevant app instance when testing push sends.
Reviewing and addressing these areas will help ensure that users who have accepted push permissions via your push primer IAM can successfully receive push notifications.[Push primer in-app messages], [Push enablement and push subscription], [Troubleshoot push notifications]"
